questions.question_english: What is the statutory prescribed rate of mandatory monthly contribution made by the Central Government / GNCTD as employer into a government employee's NPS Tier I account?
options_english: 10% of Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance
12% of Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance
14% of Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance
18.5% of Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 6 of the Central Civil Services (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2021, the rate of government contribution is statutorily fixed at 14%.

Evolution and Regulatory Provisions:
1. Historical Rate: At the inception of the National Pension System w.e.f. 01.01.2004, both the employee and the Central Government contributed equally at 10% of (Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance).
2. Enhanced Employer Share: Based on the Union Cabinet's decision and Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services) Notification dated 31.01.2019, the Central Government's monthly employer contribution was enhanced from 10% to 14% of (Basic Pay + DA), effective from 01.04.2019. The employee's mandatory contribution remained unchanged at 10%.
3. Application across Entities: This 14% statutory employer share applies to all Central Government civilian employees, Defence civilian personnel, employees of Union Territory Administrations (including GNCTD), and Central Autonomous Bodies (CABs) covered under NPS.
4. DDO Responsibilities: The DDO must compute the employer contribution strictly on (Basic Pay + DA) drawn in the monthly bill and ensure that both employee (10%) and government (14%) shares—totaling 24%—are credited simultaneously to the subscriber's PRAN through the PAO / Treasury.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (राष्ट्रीय पेंशन प्रणाली का क्रियान्वयन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 6 के तहत सरकारी अंशदान की दर सांविधिक रूप से 14% निर्धारित है।

ऐतिहासिक पृष्ठभूमि एवं वैधानिक प्रावधान:
1. प्रारंभिक दर: 01.01.2004 को NPS लागू होने के समय कर्मचारी और केंद्र सरकार दोनों का अंशदान मूल वेतन + महंगाई भत्ते (DA) के 10-10% के बराबर था।
2. नियोक्ता के हिस्से में वृद्धि: केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल के निर्णय और वित्त मंत्रालय (वित्तीय सेवाएं विभाग) की 31.01.2019 की अधिसूचना के अनुसार, 01.04.2019 से केंद्र सरकार के मासिक नियोक्ता अंशदान को 10% से बढ़ाकर 14% कर दिया गया। कर्मचारी का अनिवार्य अंशदान 10% पर ही स्थिर रखा गया।
3. प्रयोज्यता: यह 14% की दर केंद्र सरकार के सभी सिविल कर्मचारियों, केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासनों (GNCTD सहित), और केंद्र सरकार के स्वायत्त निकायों (CABs) पर अनिवार्य रूप से लागू है।
4. DDO का उत्तरदायित्व: आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) का यह वैधानिक कर्तव्य है कि वह प्रत्येक माह वेतन बिल में (मूल वेतन + DA) पर 14% सरकारी अंशदान की सही गणना करे और कर्मचारी के 10% हिस्से के साथ कुल 24% राशि प्रान (PRAN) में समय पर जमा करवाए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) 14% of Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: For government servants covered under the National Pension System, the Central Government or Union Territory Administration contributes a mandatory monthly share equal to fourteen percent of the employee’s basic pay plus applicable dearness allowance. This enhanced rate provides significant financial backing to build a robust post-retirement corpus for serving employees.

questions.question_english: Under the PFRDA exit regulations for the NPS, if the total accumulated pension wealth of a subscriber retiring at superannuation is equal to or less than a specified threshold, they are permitted to withdraw the entire corpus without purchasing an annuity. What is this threshold limit?
options_english: ₹2.5 Lakhs
₹5 Lakhs
₹10 Lakhs
₹15 Lakhs
questions.explanation_english:
Under Regulation 3(a) of the PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) Regulations, as amended in 2021:
1. Superannuation Threshold: If the total accumulated pension wealth of an NPS subscriber retiring on superannuation (or attaining the age of 60 years) is equal to or less than ₹5,00,000 (Rupees Five Lakhs), the subscriber is granted the option to withdraw the entire accumulated corpus (100%) as a lump sum without any mandatory requirement to purchase an annuity.
2. Policy Rationale: For small balances up to ₹5 Lakhs, an annuity purchase of 40% (i.e. ₹2 Lakhs) produces negligible monthly pension yields after administrative overheads; hence full liquidity is provided to the retiree.
3. Comparison with Premature Exit: For premature exits (resignation before age 60 under Regulation 4), the threshold limit for full 100% withdrawal is ₹2.5 Lakhs.
questions.explanation_hindi:
PFRDA (राष्ट्रीय पेंशन प्रणाली के अंतर्गत निकास एवं आहरण) संशोधन विनियम, 2021 के विनियम 3(क) के अनुसार:
1. अधिवर्षिता सीमा: अधिवर्षिता (60 वर्ष की आयु) पर सेवानिवृत्त होने वाले NPS अभिदाता के लिए बिना कोई वार्षिकी (annuity) खरीदे पूरी 100% संचित राशि एकमुश्त निकालने की सीमा ₹5,00,000 (पांच लाख रुपये) निर्धारित की गई है (जो पूर्व में ₹2 लाख थी)।
2. नीतिगत औचित्य: यदि कुल संचित कॉर्पस ₹5 लाख या उससे कम है, तो 40% राशि (अधिकतम ₹2 लाख) से मिलने वाली वार्षिकी (मासिक पेंशन) अत्यंत नगण्य होगी, इसलिए अभिदाता को पूरी राशि एकमुश्त निकालने की सुविधा दी गई है।
3. असामयिक निकास से तुलना: सेवा से त्यागपत्र (असामयिक निकास) के मामले में 100% एकमुश्त आहरण की यह सीमा ₹2.5 लाख है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) ₹5 Lakhs

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under PFRDA exit and withdrawal regulations, if the total accumulated pension wealth of an NPS subscriber retiring on superannuation is equal to or less than five lakh rupees, the subscriber is permitted to withdraw the entire accumulated corpus as a lump sum without any mandatory annuity purchase requirement.

questions.question_english: Under Rule 9 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, what mandatory requirement applies if a retired government officer takes up commercial employment within one year of retirement?
options_english: They must voluntarily surrender 50% of their monthly pension.
They are required to refund the entire amount of Retirement Gratuity.
They are disqualified from drawing any pension for the entire duration of the employment.
Retired Group 'A' officers must obtain prior permission from the Central Government.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 9 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (Commercial Employment after Retirement):
1. **Applicability to Group 'A' Officers:** If a pensioner who was a member of a Central Civil Service, **Group 'A'**, wishes to accept any commercial employment before the expiry of **one year** from the date of retirement, they must obtain the prior permission of the Central Government.
2. **Cooling-off Period:** The cooling-off period was originally two years under earlier rules but was amended to one year. Commercial employment includes employment in any capacity with a private firm, corporation, joint venture, or trust.
3. **Sanctions for Non-Compliance:** If a retired Group 'A' officer accepts commercial employment without obtaining prior permission, or in violation of specified conditions, the Central Government has statutory authority to order the forfeiture or withholding of pension in whole or in part, permanently or for a specified duration.
4. **Conflict of Interest Check:** The competent cadre-controlling ministry examines whether the officer had official dealings with the prospective employer during the preceding three years of service.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 9 (सेवानिवृत्ति के बाद वाणिज्यिक नियोजन) के अनुसार:
1. **समूह 'क' अधिकारियों के लिए अनिवार्यता:** यदि कोई पेंशनभोगी, जो अपनी सेवानिवृत्ति से ठीक पहले **समूह 'क' (Group 'A')** सेवा का अधिकारी था, अपनी सेवानिवृत्ति की तिथि से **एक वर्ष** की अवधि समाप्त होने से पूर्व कोई वाणिज्यिक नियोजन स्वीकार करना चाहता है, तो उसे केंद्र सरकार की पूर्वानुमति लेना अनिवार्य है।
2. **कूलिंग-ऑफ अवधि:** पूर्ववर्ती नियमों में यह कूलिंग-ऑफ अवधि दो वर्ष थी, जिसे बाद में घटाकर एक वर्ष कर दिया गया है। वाणिज्यिक नियोजन में किसी निजी कंपनी, ट्रस्ट अथवा फर्म में किसी भी पद पर कार्य करना शामिल है।
3. **उल्लंघन पर दंड:** यदि कोई सेवानिवृत्त समूह 'क' अधिकारी पूर्वानुमति के बिना ऐसा नियोजन स्वीकार करता है, तो सरकार उसकी पेंशन को पूर्णतः या आंशिक रूप से रोकने अथवा समाप्त करने का आदेश दे सकती है।
4. **हितों के टकराव की जांच:** सरकार यह सुनिश्चित करती है कि अधिकारी ने सेवानिवृत्ति से पूर्व के अंतिम 3 वर्षों के दौरान संबंधित निजी कंपनी के साथ कोई अनुचित आधिकारिक लेन-देन तो नहीं किया था।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Group A officers must obtain prior permission from the Government.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, a retired Group A officer who wishes to accept commercial employment within one year of retirement must obtain prior written permission from the Central Government. Accepting commercial employment without required sanction may lead to withholding or forfeiture of pensionary benefits.

questions.question_english: The formula to calculate ‘Service Gratuity’ for an employee retiring with less than 10 years of qualifying service under OPS is:
options_english: Half a month’s emoluments per completed six-monthly service period.
One full month’s emoluments for every completed year of continuous service.
One-fourth of a month’s emoluments for every completed year of qualifying service.
A fixed maximum lump-sum compensation amount of ₹1 Lakh regardless of pay.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 44 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 49(1) of the 1972 Rules):
1. A government servant who retires from service before completing the minimum qualifying service of 10 years (20 completed six-monthly periods) is not eligible for a recurring monthly pension.
2. In lieu of pension, the employee is granted a one-time lump-sum terminal compensation designated as 'Service Gratuity'.
3. The statutory rate of Service Gratuity is half a month's emoluments (Basic Pay + DA) for every completed six-monthly period of qualifying service.
(Note: This is separate from and in addition to Retirement Gratuity under Rule 45, which is payable at 1/4th of emoluments per completed six-monthly period after 5 years of qualifying service).
Therefore, Service Gratuity is calculated at half a month's emoluments per completed six-monthly period. Hence, option A is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 44 (पूर्ववर्ती 1972 नियमावली के नियम 49(1)) के अनुसार:
1. यदि कोई सरकारी कर्मचारी 10 वर्ष (20 छमाही) की न्यूनतम अर्हक सेवा पूरी किए बिना सेवानिवृत्त होता है, तो वह नियमित मासिक पेंशन का पात्र नहीं होता है।
2. पेंशन के बदले ऐसे कर्मचारी को एकमुश्त 'सेवा उपदान' (Service Gratuity) प्रदान किया जाता है।
3. सेवा उपदान की गणना का वैधानिक सूत्र: अर्हक सेवा की प्रत्येक पूर्ण 6-मासिक (छमाही) अवधि के लिए आधे महीने की परिलब्धियां (मूल वेतन + महंगाई भत्ता) है।
(ध्यान दें: यह नियम 45 के तहत मिलने वाली सेवानिवृत्ति ग्रेच्युटी से भिन्न है, जिसकी दर प्रति छमाही 1/4 परिलब्धियां होती है और जो 5 वर्ष की सेवा पूरी होने पर देय होती है)।
अतः सेवा उपदान की सही गणना दर प्रति छमाही आधा महीना (Half a month's emoluments) है। सही उत्तर A है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Half a month’s emoluments per completed six-monthly service period.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When a government servant retires under OPS with less than ten years of qualifying service, no monthly pension is payable. Instead, they receive a Service Gratuity calculated at the rate of half a month’s emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service rendered in government service.

questions.explanation_english:
Under the financial architecture of the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS):
1. Government Contribution: To guarantee an assured pension of 50%, an assured minimum pension of ₹10,000, Dearness Relief indexation, and assured family pension without making the scheme unfunded, the Central Government's contribution has been substantially increased from 14% of (Basic Pay + DA) to 18.5% of (Basic Pay + DA).

1. सरकारी अंशदान: 50% की सुनिश्चित पेंशन, ₹10,000 की न्यूनतम सुनिश्चित पेंशन, महंगाई राहत (DR) और सुनिश्चित पारिवारिक पेंशन जैसी गारंटियों को वित्तीय रूप से वहनीय बनाने के लिए, केंद्र सरकार के मासिक अंशदान को (मूल वेतन + DA) के 14% से बढ़ाकर 18.5% कर दिया गया है।

3. ऐतिहासिक परिप्रेक्ष्य: 2004 में एनपीएस की शुरुआत में कर्मचारी और सरकार दोनों का अंशदान 10% था। 01.04.2019 से सरकार का अंशदान बढ़ाकर 14% किया गया था। अब UPS के तहत इसे बढ़ाकर 18.5% किया गया है।
अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प C (18.5%) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) 18.5%

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: To fund the financial guarantees and structural benefits offered under the Unified Pension Scheme, the government’s monthly contribution toward the employee’s pension fund is increased from fourteen percent to eighteen point five percent of basic pay plus dearness allowance, while the employee contribution remains unchanged at ten percent.

questions.question_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियमावली के प्रशासनिक और विधिक संदर्भ में, 'बॉय सर्विस' (Boy Service) शब्द विशेष रूप से किस आयु को प्राप्त करने से पूर्व की गई सेवा को संदर्भित करता है?

Inflation-indexed single life annuity increasing automatically by a fixed rate of 5% annually throughout life.
questions.explanation_english:
Under the PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) Regulations:
1. Statutory Default Annuity Scheme: For government sector subscribers exiting the National Pension System on superannuation, the statutory default annuity scheme is: "Annuity for life of the subscriber with a provision for 100% annuity payable to the spouse for life on the demise of the subscriber, and with a provision for return of the purchase price (ROP) to the nominee / legal heirs of the subscriber upon the death of the spouse (last survivor)".
2. Alignment with Family Pension Principles: This default variant is designed to mirror the security provided by family pensions under the traditional pension rules, ensuring that the surviving spouse does not face financial distress or a reduced pension upon the employee's demise, while safeguarding the capital for the heirs.
3. Voluntary Alternative: The subscriber has the freedom to choose any other annuity variant (such as annuity without return of purchase price or single life annuity) if they actively elect to do so in the exit application.

questions.question_english: In cases where an employee disappears, the family can apply for family pension and death gratuity after the stipulated time frame. What condition must the family fulfill regarding the death gratuity?
options_english: They must surrender 50% of the calculated gratuity amount to government treasury immediately.
They must purchase an NPS life annuity using the full accumulated gratuity amount received.
They must formally secure an explicit authorization order from the Supreme Court of India.
Execute an indemnity bond with two sureties to refund if employee reappears.
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (and consolidated DoP&PW guidelines regarding missing employees/pensioners), when a government servant disappears leaving no trace, the family must first lodge a formal First Information Report (FIR) with the police. If after an investigation of at least six months the police submit an untraced report certifying that the employee cannot be located, the family becomes eligible to apply for family pension, retirement-cum-death gratuity, leave encashment, and GPF balances.

However, regarding the payment of death gratuity (and arrears of family pension), the sanctioning authority requires the beneficiary/claimant to execute a formal Indemnity Bond (Form Annexure) supported by two solvent sureties. This indemnity bond legally binds the recipients to refund to the Government the full amount of gratuity and pension paid to them if the missing government servant subsequently reappears alive or is proved to have been alive during that period. This safeguards public funds while providing immediate social security and financial relief to the distressed family.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 तथा कार्मिक, लोक शिकायत और पेंशन मंत्रालय (DoP&PW) के समेकित दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार, जब कोई सरकारी कर्मचारी अचानक लापता हो जाता है, तो उसके परिवार को सर्वप्रथम स्थानीय पुलिस में प्राथमिकी (FIR) दर्ज करानी होती है। यदि कम से कम छह महीने की निर्धारित समय-सीमा बीतने के बाद पुलिस 'अप्राप्य रिपोर्ट' (Untraced Report) प्रस्तुत करती है, तो परिवार पारिवारिक पेंशन और मृत्यु उपदान (Death Gratuity) के लिए आवेदन करने का पात्र बन जाता है।

मृत्यु उपदान के भुगतान की एक अनिवार्य वैधानिक पूर्व-शर्त यह है कि दावेदार परिवार को दो सक्षम/सॉल्वेंट प्रतिभुओं (Sureties) द्वारा समर्थित एक क्षतिपूर्ति बंधपत्र (Indemnity Bond) निष्पादित करना होता है। यह बंधपत्र सरकार को यह कानूनी गारंटी देता है कि यदि लापता कर्मचारी भविष्य में जीवित पुनः प्रकट हो जाता है, तो परिवार को भुगतान की गई उपदान और पेंशन राशि सरकारी खजाने में वापस लौटानी होगी। यह प्रक्रिया सरकारी धन की सुरक्षा और संकटग्रस्त परिवार को त्वरित वित्तीय संबल प्रदान करने के बीच संतुलन स्थापित करती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Execute an indemnity bond with two sureties

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When an employee disappears and the family applies for death gratuity and family pension after six months, the family must execute an indemnity bond supported by two solvent sureties. This legal bond guarantees that the family will refund the payments if the missing employee subsequently reappears alive.

questions.question_english: What is the statutory treatment of the accumulated Tier-I pension wealth of a Central Government employee covered under the National Pension System (NPS) upon their dismissal or removal from service?

questions.explanation_english: Under Regulation 6 of the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) Regulations, 2015, and the CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021, when an NPS-covered government servant is dismissed or removed from service, the exit from the system is legally classified and processed as a 'premature exit' (exit before the age of superannuation). Unlike the Old Pension Scheme where past service is forfeited, the individual's proprietary NPS Tier-I accumulated pension corpus is not forfeited. Under premature exit provisions, the subscriber must utilize at least 80% of the accumulated pension wealth to purchase a life annuity from an Annuity Service Provider (ASP), and a maximum of 20% can be withdrawn as a lump sum. (If the total corpus is ₹2.5 lakh or less, 100% lump sum withdrawal is permissible).

questions.question_english: Which of the following entities are officially authorized and empanelled by the PFRDA to disburse regular periodic annuity payments to exiting NPS subscribers?
options_english: Any nationalized or scheduled commercial bank operating in India
Registered Pension Fund Managers (PFMs) such as SBI Pension Funds

questions.explanation_english:
Under the PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) Regulations:
1. Annuity Service Providers (ASPs): PFRDA empanels designated Life Insurance Companies (such as Life Insurance Corporation of India, SBI Life, HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential Life, etc.) that are registered with and regulated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) to act as Annuity Service Providers (ASPs).
2. Mechanism: When an NPS subscriber superannuates or exits from the scheme, a statutory portion of the accumulated corpus (at least 40% on normal superannuation, and at least 80% on premature voluntary exit) is utilized to purchase an annuity contract from an empanelled ASP chosen by the subscriber.
3. Distinct Roles: Pension Fund Managers (PFMs) only manage investment portfolios during the accumulation phase; the Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA) maintains accounts and records; and Banks handle remittance and nodal transactions. Only empanelled ASPs are authorized to disburse monthly annuity/pension payments.

questions.question_english: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the pensionary entitlements of a Central Government employee who is dismissed or removed from service under the Old Pension Scheme (CCS Pension Rules)?
options_english: They forfeit all claims to pension and gratuity, though a compassionate allowance not exceeding two-thirds may be sanctioned in deserving cases.
They remain fully entitled to receive their monthly superannuation pension but permanently forfeit their retirement gratuity.
They automatically receive a statutory minimum guaranteed pension equal to 50% of the pension otherwise admissible on the date of exit.
The disciplinary penalty of dismissal affects only active employment and future increments, leaving accrued pensionary entitlements untouched.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 23 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 24 of the 1972 Rules), dismissal or removal of a government servant from a service or post entails forfeiture of their past service, which extinguishes all claims to pension and retirement gratuity. However, under Rule 41 of CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, the competent disciplinary authority may, if the case is deserving of special consideration on compassionate grounds, sanction a 'Compassionate Allowance' not exceeding two-thirds of the pension, gratuity, or both, which would have been admissible had the government servant retired on invalid pension. The compassionate allowance cannot be claimed as a matter of right and must not fall below the minimum pension floor (currently ₹9,000 per month).
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 23 (पूर्ववर्ती 1972 नियमों का नियम 24) के अनुसार, किसी सरकारी सेवक की सेवा या पद से बर्खास्तगी (dismissal) या निष्कासन (removal) के परिणामस्वरूप उसकी पिछली समस्त सेवा जब्त (forfeited) हो जाती है, जिससे पेंशन और उपदान के सभी दावों का लोप हो जाता है। तथापि, नियम 41 के अंतर्गत यह प्रावधान है कि यदि मामला अनुकंपा के आधार पर विशेष विचार के योग्य है, तो बर्खास्त या हटाने वाला सक्षम प्राधिकारी उस पेंशन या उपदान अथवा दोनों के दो-तिहाई (2/3) से अनधिक 'अनुकंपा भत्ता' (Compassionate Allowance) स्वीकृत कर सकता है, जो उसे अशक्तता पेंशन (invalid pension) पर सेवानिवृत्त होने पर अनुज्ञेय होती। यह भत्ता न्यूनतम पेंशन (₹9,000 प्रति माह) से कम नहीं हो सकता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) They forfeit pension and gratuity, but compassionate allowance (up to 2/3rds) may be granted.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: compassionate allowance (up to 2/3rds) may be granted. When a government servant is dismissed or removed from service, they forfeit all claims to pension and gratuity. However, if the case deserves special consideration on compassionate grounds, the competent authority may grant a compassionate allowance not exceeding two- thirds of the pension and gratuity that would have been admissible.

questions.question_english: Under the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, what is the minimum qualifying service required for a government servant covered by the OPS to be eligible for a full monthly retirement pension (at 50% of emoluments or average emoluments)?
options_english: 33 years
25 years
20 years
10 years
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 44 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, the minimum qualifying service required for eligibility to receive a full retirement pension is 10 years.

Statutory Evolution and Key Rules:
1. Delinking of Full Pension from 33 Years: Prior to 01.01.2006 (under the 5th Pay Commission recommendations), a government servant needed 33 years of qualifying service to earn a full pension (50% of emoluments), and pensions were prorated downwards for service between 10 and 33 years. Following the 6th CPC recommendations (accepted w.e.f. 01.01.2006) and incorporated into Rule 44 of CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, full pension was delinked from 33 years of service.
2. Current 10-Year Threshold: Once a government servant completes a minimum qualifying service of 10 years (or 20 completed six-monthly periods of qualifying service), they become eligible to receive the full pension calculated at 50% of emoluments or 50% of average emoluments, whichever is higher.
3. Less than 10 Years Service: If a government servant retires with less than 10 years of qualifying service, they are not entitled to any monthly pension. In such cases, only a one-time lump sum Service Gratuity (at the rate of half a month's emoluments for every completed six-monthly period of qualifying service) is granted under Rule 44(1).
4. Retirement Gratuity Distinction: Minimum qualifying service for Retirement Gratuity is 5 years, whereas for full monthly pension it is 10 years.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 44 के तहत, पूर्ण मासिक सेवानिवृत्ति पेंशन प्राप्त करने के लिए न्यूनतम अर्हक सेवा (Qualifying Service) 10 वर्ष है।

ऐतिहासिक परिवर्तन एवं सांविधिक नियम:
1. 33 वर्ष की सेवा की अनिवार्यता की समाप्ति: 01.01.2006 से पहले (5वें वेतन आयोग तक), पूर्ण पेंशन (50%) प्राप्त करने के लिए 33 वर्ष की अर्हक सेवा अनिवार्य थी और 10 से 33 वर्ष की सेवा पर आनुपातिक (Prorated) पेंशन दी जाती थी। लेकिन 6वें वेतन आयोग की सिफारिशों के आधार पर 01.01.2006 से 33 वर्ष की शर्त समाप्त कर दी गई, जिसे सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 44 में संहिताबद्ध किया गया है।
2. वर्तमान 10 वर्ष की सीमा: अब यदि किसी सरकारी कर्मचारी ने न्यूनतम 10 वर्ष (अर्थात 20 छमाही अवधियां) की अर्हक सेवा पूर्ण कर ली है, तो वह अंतिम वेतन या औसत उपलब्धियों के पूरे 50% की दर से पूर्ण पेंशन प्राप्त करने का हकदार हो जाता है।
3. 10 वर्ष से कम सेवा का परिणाम: यदि किसी कर्मचारी की अर्हक सेवा 10 वर्ष से कम है, तो वह मासिक पेंशन के लिए पात्र नहीं होता है। ऐसी स्थिति में नियम 44(1) के तहत केवल एकमुश्त 'सेवा उपदान' (Service Gratuity) प्रदान किया जाता है (प्रत्येक पूर्ण छमाही सेवा के लिए आधे महीने के वेतन की दर से)।
4. सेवानिवृत्ति उपदान (Retirement Gratuity) से अंतर: सेवानिवृत्ति उपदान के लिए न्यूनतम अर्हक सेवा 5 वर्ष होती है, जबकि मासिक पेंशन के लिए न्यूनतम 10 वर्ष है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) 10 years

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, a government servant covered by the Old Pension Scheme must complete a minimum qualifying service of ten years to become eligible for a monthly retirement pension. If qualifying service is less than ten years, only a lump-sum service gratuity is granted upon exit.

questions.question_english: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding the eligibility of dependent parents for family pension under the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021:
options_english: Dependent parents become eligible only if the deceased government servant left behind no eligible widow/widower or eligible child.
Dependent parents are eligible to share the family pension equally with the surviving spouse of the deceased.
The mother receives the family pension first, and upon her death, the father becomes eligible.
The statutory income criterion for dependency applies to the parents.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 50(9)(f) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, dependent parents are positioned in the hierarchy of family pension beneficiaries strictly after the spouse and eligible children. Family pension cannot be shared between dependent parents and a surviving spouse. Dependent parents become eligible only when the deceased government servant leaves behind no eligible surviving widow/widower, no eligible disabled child, and no eligible child under the age of 25 / eligible unmarried daughter. When parents become eligible, the family pension is sanctioned first to the mother; after her demise, it is sanctioned to the father, provided they were wholly dependent on the government servant at the time of death (i.e. their combined monthly income does not exceed ₹9,000/- plus DR). Therefore, statement B is completely incorrect and represents the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 50(9)(f) के अनुसार, आश्रित माता-पिता पारिवारिक पेंशन के लाभार्थियों के पदानुक्रम में जीवनसाथी और बच्चों के बाद आते हैं। आश्रित माता-पिता को जीवित पति या पत्नी के साथ पारिवारिक पेंशन को साझा (share) करने का कोई कानूनी अधिकार नहीं है। माता-पिता पारिवारिक पेंशन के लिए केवल तभी पात्र होते हैं जब मृतक कर्मचारी के पीछे कोई पात्र विधवा/विधुर अथवा कोई पात्र संतान (25 वर्ष से कम आयु का पुत्र/दिव्यांग संतान/अविवाहित पुत्री) न बची हो। यदि दोनों माता-पिता पात्र हैं, तो पहले माता को पारिवारिक पेंशन मिलती है और उनकी मृत्यु के पश्चात पिता को दी जाती है, बशर्ते उनकी आय न्यूनतम पेंशन (₹9,000 + DR) से कम हो। अतः कथन B पूर्णतः असत्य है और यही सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Dependent parents are eligible to share the family pension equally with the surviving spouse of the deceased.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Dependent parents do not share family pension equally with a surviving spouse. Under pension rules, dependent parents become eligible for family pension only when the deceased employee leaves behind no eligible surviving spouse or eligible children. The mother receives family pension first, followed by the father upon her demise, subject to dependency.

questions.question_english: What is the role of a ‘Nominee’ in the GPF rules?
options_english: To operate and manage the GPF account on behalf of a medically incapacitated subscriber.
To act as a legal financial guarantor whenever the subscriber applies for a GPF advance.
To decide and alter the market investment pattern of the accumulated GPF funds.
To receive accumulated GPF balance upon the subscriber’s death.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 5 and Rule 33 of the General Provident Fund (Central Services) Rules, 1960, every subscriber joining the fund is statutorily required to execute a nomination conferring on one or more persons the right to receive the amount standing to their credit in the fund in the event of their death while in service or before the amount has become payable or has been paid. The primary legal role of a designated nominee is to serve as the authorized beneficiary entitled to receive and claim the accumulated financial balance and interest in the subscriber’s GPF account upon their demise. A nominee has no right to operate the account during the subscriber's lifetime, nor do they act as guarantors or make investment choices. Hence, option D is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्य भविष्य निधि (केंद्रीय सेवाएं) नियम, 1960 के नियम 5 और नियम 33 के अनुसार, प्रत्येक अभिदाता के लिए निधि में शामिल होते समय एक नामांकन (Nomination) प्रस्तुत करना अनिवार्य है। इस नामांकन का एकमात्र विधिक उद्देश्य यह है कि यदि अभिदाता की सेवाकाल के दौरान अथवा GPF राशि का भुगतान होने से पूर्व मृत्यु हो जाती है, तो उसके खाते में जमा संचित राशि और उस पर अर्जित ब्याज को प्राप्त करने का अधिकार नामित व्यक्ति (Nominee) को प्राप्त होता है। नामिनी जीवित अभिदाता के खाते का संचालन नहीं कर सकता और न ही वह किसी ऋण का गारंटर होता है। GPF सरकारी निधि है जिसमें वित्त मंत्रालय द्वारा ब्याज तय होता है, अतः इसमें बाजार निवेश का कोई विकल्प नहीं होता। सही उत्तर D है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) To receive accumulated GPF balance upon the subscriber’s death.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the General Provident Fund Rules, the primary legal role of a designated nominee is to receive the accumulated financial balance standing to the credit of the subscriber’s GPF account in the event of the subscriber’s death during active service or prior to receiving final account settlement.

questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 62 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 69 of the erstwhile 1972 Rules):
1. **Sanctioning Authority:** Where departmental or judicial proceedings are pending against a government servant on their retirement date, the **Head of the Department (HoD)** is the designated competent authority to sanction provisional pension.
2. **Amount of Provisional Pension:** The provisional pension is sanctioned for an amount equal to the maximum pension admissible on the basis of qualifying service up to the date of retirement (or the date immediately preceding suspension, if suspended at retirement).
3. **Provisional Gratuity Prohibited:** No gratuity (retirement or death gratuity) shall be paid until the final conclusion of the proceedings and issue of final orders.
4. **Validity:** Provisional pension continues to be drawn until final orders are issued by the competent authority concluding the proceedings.

3. **उपदान का निषेध:** कार्यवाही समाप्त होने और सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा अंतिम आदेश जारी किए जाने तक सेवानिवृत्ति उपदान (Gratuity) का कोई भी हिस्सा संवितरित नहीं किया जाता।

questions.question_english: Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, what is the consequence on qualifying service if a government servant resigns from service (other than a technical resignation to take up another approved government appointment)?
options_english: The past qualifying service is protected, and pension is granted on a pro-rata basis upon attaining 60 years of age.
The employee receives a lump-sum severance gratuity equal to one month's emoluments for each completed year of service.
Fifty percent of the past service is credited towards deferred pension benefits under special relaxation.
Resignation entails complete forfeiture of all past service, resulting in no pensionary or retirement gratuity benefits.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 26(1) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 26(1) of the erstwhile CCS Pension Rules, 1972), resignation from a service or a post entails forfeiture of past service. When a government servant resigns voluntarily from public service for private reasons or without statutory permission, all past qualifying service rendered by the employee is forfeited entirely. Consequently, the individual becomes ineligible for superannuation pension, retiring pension, retirement gratuity, or commutation of pension. The only statutory exception is provided under Rule 26(2), known as 'Technical Resignation', where an employee resigns with prior official permission from the competent authority to take up another appointment under the Government of India or an eligible autonomous body where service qualifies for pension. In a technical resignation, the past qualifying service is carried forward and counted towards pensionary benefits in the new department. For a Head of Office (HOO) or school Principal, whenever an employee tenders a resignation, the HOO must verify whether proper permission was obtained for outside employment through proper channel to categorize it as technical resignation; otherwise, the resignation is treated as ordinary resignation resulting in complete forfeiture of past service.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 26(1) (पूर्ववर्ती सीसीएस पेंशन नियम, 1972 के नियम 26(1)) के अनुसार, किसी पद या सेवा से त्यागपत्र (Resignation) देने पर पिछली समस्त सेवा का समपहरण (Forfeiture of past service) हो जाता है। जब कोई सरकारी कर्मचारी व्यक्तिगत कारणों से या बिना पूर्वानुमति के सेवा से त्यागपत्र देता है, तो उसकी पिछली समस्त अर्हक सेवा पूर्णतः शून्य मान ली जाती है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप वह किसी भी पेंशन, सेवानिवृत्ति उपदान (Retirement Gratuity) अथवा पेंशन संराशीकरण (Commutation) का हकदार नहीं रहता। इसका एकमात्र वैधानिक अपवाद नियम 26(2) के अंतर्गत 'तकनीकी त्यागपत्र' (Technical Resignation) है। यदि कर्मचारी ने सक्षम प्राधिकारी की पूर्व अनुमति से और उचित माध्यम से केंद्र सरकार के किसी अन्य पात्र विभाग या सेवा में पदभार ग्रहण करने हेतु त्यागपत्र दिया हो, तो पिछली सेवा जब्त नहीं होती बल्कि वह नई सेवा में पेंशन प्रयोजनार्थ जोड़ी जाती है। कार्यालय प्रमुख (HOO) अथवा प्राचार्य को त्यागपत्र स्वीकार करते समय यह स्पष्ट रूप से अभिलेखित करना अनिवार्य होता है कि त्यागपत्र सामान्य है या तकनीकी, क्योंकि सामान्य त्यागपत्र समस्त पेंशनरी लाभों को स्थायी रूप से समाप्त कर देता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Resignation entails the forfeiture of all past service, resulting in no pensionary benefits.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, resignation from a post or service entails forfeiture of all past service rendered by the employee. Unless the resignation qualifies as a technical resignation to take up another approved government appointment, the former employee forfeits all rights to receive pension, gratuity, and related pensionary terminal benefits.

questions.question_english: If a subscriber under NPS wishes to increase their equity exposure limit in their Tier I account (Active Choice), what is the maximum percentage allowed for government employees as per current PFRDA norms?
questions.explanation_english:
In 2019, the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, along with PFRDA, introduced significant investment flexibility for Central Government employees enrolled under the National Pension System (NPS):

1. Default Pattern: If no choice is exercised, contributions are invested across PFMs under a regulated mix (up to 15% equity, with remaining in government securities and corporate debt).
2. Active Choice: Central Government subscribers are allowed to select their own Pension Fund Manager (PFM) and allocate their pension contributions across three Asset Classes:
   - Asset Class G (Government Securities): Up to 100%
   - Asset Class C (Corporate Debt Instruments): Up to 100%
   - Asset Class E (Equity and Equity-related instruments): Maximum ceiling of 50%
3. Auto Choice: Subscribers can opt for lifecycle funds: Conservative (LC-25, max 25% equity) or Moderate (LC-50, max 50% equity tapering with age).

While private/all-citizen sector subscribers can allocate up to 75% in equity under Active Choice, the statutory ceiling for government sector subscribers remains strictly capped at 50% for Asset Class E.

वर्ष 2019 में वित्तीय सेवाएं विभाग (DFS), वित्त मंत्रालय तथा पीएफआरडीए (PFRDA) ने राष्ट्रीय पेंशन प्रणाली (NPS) के तहत आने वाले केंद्र सरकार के कर्मचारियों के लिए निवेश विकल्पों में महत्वपूर्ण लचीलापन प्रदान किया:

1. डिफ़ॉल्ट विकल्प (Default Choice): यदि कोई विकल्प नहीं चुना जाता है, तो अंशदान सरकारी दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार निवेश किया जाता है (जिसमें इक्विटी का हिस्सा अधिकतम 15% तक होता है)।
2. सक्रिय विकल्प (Active Choice): सरकारी अभिदाता अपनी पसंद का पेंशन फंड मैनेजर चुन सकते हैं और निम्नलिखित परिसंपत्ति वर्गों में निवेश आवंटित कर सकते हैं:
   - एसेट क्लास G (सरकारी प्रतिभूतियां): 100% तक
   - एसेट क्लास C (कॉर्पोरेट बॉन्ड/ऋण साधन): 100% तक
   - एसेट क्लास E (इक्विटी / शेयर बाजार): अधिकतम 50% तक
3. ऑटो विकल्प (Auto Choice): अभिदाता दो लाइफ-साइकिल फंड चुन सकते हैं - LC-25 (अधिकतम 25% इक्विटी) या LC-50 (अधिकतम 50% इक्विटी जो उम्र बढ़ने के साथ घटती है)।

यद्यपि गैर-सरकारी/निजी क्षेत्र के नागरिकों के लिए सक्रिय विकल्प में इक्विटी की सीमा 75% तक है, परंतु केंद्र सरकार के कर्मचारियों के लिए परिसंपत्ति वर्ग E में अधिकतम सीमा 50% निर्धारित है।

questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 39 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, an 'Invalid Pension' is granted to a government servant who is retired from service on account of any bodily or mental infirmity which permanently incapacitates them for service. The incapacitation must be certified by an appropriately constituted Medical Board (or Civil Surgeon / District Medical Officer, as specified in the rules). This pension ensures statutory social security and income replacement for government employees who are forced to exit government service prematurely on medical grounds. In contrast:
- Compensation Pension (Rule 40) is granted when an employee is discharged due to the abolition of a permanent post.
- Retiring Pension (Rule 35) is granted upon voluntary retirement or premature retirement after completing specified qualifying service.
- Compassionate Allowance (Rule 42) is granted at the discretion of the competent authority to an employee dismissed or removed from service.

questions.question_english: Under which rule of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 can the President reserve the right of withholding a pension or ordering recovery from a pension?
options_english: Rule 8
Rule 14
Rule 39
Rule 65
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, Rule 8 comprehensively consolidates the provisions governing the President's prerogative over pensions:

1. Future Good Conduct: Rule 8(1) lays down that future good conduct shall be an implied condition of every grant of pension and its continuance.
2. Power of the President: Rule 8(2) explicitly provides that the President reserves the right of withholding a pension or gratuity, or both, either in full or in part, or withdrawing a pension in full or in part, whether permanently or for a specified period, and of ordering recovery from a pension or gratuity of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused to the Government, if the pensioner is found guilty of grave misconduct or negligence during their service in any departmental or judicial proceedings.

Note on 1972 vs 2021 Rules:
In the older CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972, this power was bifurcated between Rule 8 (good conduct) and Rule 9 (President's right to withhold or withdraw pension). In the updated CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, these powers have been consolidated under Rule 8.
- Rule 14 relates to the commencement and conditions of qualifying service.
- Rule 39 relates to superannuation pension.
- Rule 65 relates to recovery and adjustment of government dues.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 8 के तहत राष्ट्रपति का पेंशन रोकने, वापस लेने या उससे सरकारी नुकसान की वसूली कराने का वैधानिक अधिकार निर्धारित किया गया है:

1. भावी सदाचार की शर्त: नियम 8(1) के अनुसार, भविष्य में अच्छा आचरण (Future good conduct) पेंशन की स्वीकृति और उसके निरंतर जारी रहने की एक अंतर्निहित शर्त है।
2. राष्ट्रपति का अधिकार: नियम 8(2) यह प्रावधान करता है कि यदि किसी विभागीय या न्यायिक कार्यवाही में पेंशनभोगी को अपनी सेवा अवधि के दौरान गंभीर कदाचार (Grave Misconduct) या घोर लापरवाही (Negligence) का दोषी पाया जाता है, तो राष्ट्रपति को पेंशन या उपदान (या दोनों) को पूर्णतः या आंशिक रूप से, स्थायी रूप से या किसी निश्चित अवधि के लिए रोकने/वापस लेने का, तथा सरकार को हुए किसी भी वित्तीय नुकसान की पूरी या आंशिक वसूली का आदेश देने का अधिकार सुरक्षित है।

questions.question_english: A pensioner wants to change their bank account from which they draw their monthly pension (from a Delhi branch to a Mumbai branch of the same bank). Who processes this transfer?
options_english: The local Head of Office or School Principal directly
The Directorate of Education pension administration cell
CPAO or the authorized bank’s CPPC
The Pay and Accounts Office (PAO) having jurisdiction
questions.explanation_english:
Under the 'Scheme for Payment of Pensions to Central Government Civil Pensioners by Authorised Banks' formulated by the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, and administered by the Central Pension Accounting Office (CPAO):

1. Intra-Bank Transfer (Between branches of the same authorized bank): When a pensioner relocates and requests a transfer of pension payment from one branch to another branch of the same bank (even located in different cities or states, such as Delhi to Mumbai), the application is submitted directly to the pensioner's current paying branch. The transfer is executed centrally by the bank's Centralized Pension Processing Centre (CPPC). The CPPC updates the BSR code/branch details in its master database and notifies CPAO electronically.
2. Inter-Bank Transfer (Between two different banks): If the pensioner wishes to change the bank itself (e.g., from SBI to PNB), the CPPC returns the disinvested Pension Payment Order (PPO) to the CPAO, and CPAO issues a fresh Special Seal Authority (SSA) to the CPPC of the new receiving bank.
3. The parent Head of Office (HoO) / school principal and the field PAO do not handle routine branch/account transfers post-retirement once the PPO is operationalized.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय पेंशन लेखा कार्यालय (CPAO) तथा वित्त मंत्रालय द्वारा अधिकृत बैंकों के माध्यम से सिविल पेंशनभोगियों को पेंशन भुगतान की योजना के अनुसार:

1. एक ही बैंक की दो शाखाओं के मध्य स्थानांतरण: यदि कोई पेंशनभोगी अपने पेंशन खाते को उसी अधिकृत बैंक की एक शाखा से दूसरी शाखा में (चाहे वे दिल्ली और मुंबई जैसे अलग-अलग शहरों/राज्यों में हों) स्थानांतरित करना चाहता है, तो इसके लिए मूल स्कूल, कार्यालयाध्यक्ष या क्षेत्रीय PAO के पास जाने की आवश्यकता नहीं होती। पेंशनभोगी अपनी वर्तमान शाखा में आवेदन करता है और संबंधित अधिकृत बैंक का केंद्रीकृत पेंशन प्रसंस्करण केंद्र (Centralized Pension Processing Centre - CPPC) अपने केंद्रीय डेटाबेस में शाखा कोड (BSR Code) और खाता विवरण अद्यतन कर इसे निष्पादित करता है तथा CPAO को सूचित करता है।
2. अलग बैंकों के मध्य स्थानांतरण: यदि स्थानांतरण एक बैंक से दूसरे बैंक (जैसे SBI से पंजाब नेशनल बैंक) में हो, तो प्रक्रिया CPAO के माध्यम से नए विशेष मुहर प्राधिकार (Special Seal Authority - SSA) के तहत संपन्न की जाती है।

अतः पेंशन खाता स्थानांतरण की यह प्रक्रिया CPAO अथवा अधिकृत बैंक के CPPC द्वारा ही संसाधित की जाती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) CPAO or the authorized bank’s CPPC

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When a pensioner requests to transfer their pension payment account from one branch to another branch of the same bank across states, the process is handled through the Central Pension Accounting Office or the authorized bank’s Centralized Pension Processing Centre without requiring fresh pension sanction proceedings from the original school.
